body.heading: Look for the exact moment it goes wrong
paragraphs: “I never manage to practise” is too big to fix. But habits rarely fail everywhere at once. They fail at one particular moment: the shoes are upstairs, the app needs an update, the chosen time collides with the school run.
Replay the last few attempts slowly and find the precise point where it unravelled. That point — not your motivation — is the thing to repair.

body.heading: Common breaks and simple repairs
paragraphs: If the habit depends on something being ready, prepare it the night before or keep a spare: spare headphones, a second notebook, the mat already unrolled. If the time keeps getting eaten, move the habit earlier or attach it to something immovable, like a meal.
If the habit is simply too big for your current life, that is a design fault too. Halve it without ceremony. A smaller habit that happens beats a grand one that exists mainly as a source of guilt.

body.heading: Test the repair like a scientist
paragraphs: Change one thing, then give it a week. If the habit flows again, you found the break. If not, look for the next awkward moment. Each repair teaches you something true about how your days actually run.
Over time this way of thinking becomes the habit underneath all the others: when something slips, you reach for a spanner, not for self-criticism.

takeaway: A slipping habit usually needs a repair, not a reprimand.
